topic: Changes in Solid Materials When Bent or Pressed
key_concepts: Solid materials have definite shape and volume.
Solid materials have properties such as size, shape, color, texture, and weight.
Solid materials can be changed by cutting, tearing, folding, twisting, bending, stretching
Applying force to solid materials does not form a new material.
Bending solid materials can change their size and shape.
Pressing solid materials can change their size and shape.
Pressing some solid materials can also change their texture.
Only physical appearance changes when solid materials are bent or pressed.
Not all solid materials can be bent; bendability depends on the material.
Bending is used in industry, such as bending steel bars and making vehicle parts.
Examples of bendable materials include plastic rulers, wire, paper clips, metal spoons, an
Examples of pressable materials include modeling clay, salt, banana, pandesal, and cotton
